editorial.headline: Special Passenger Transport: Fixed-Route Mobility, Nationally Open
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers organised passenger services with fixed origins or destinations, from employee and school transport to shuttles serving stations, ports and airports.
editorial.body:
Special Passenger Transport is the category for organised passenger journeys that begin or end at a fixed point. Its practical territory is familiar: pick-up and drop-off services, employee transport, residential transport and services that connect passengers between transport modes. It also expressly includes operating school vehicles or buses, employee pick-up vehicles or buses, and shuttle buses serving stations, ports or airports. The defining feature is not simply that passengers are moved, but that the service is structured around a settled origin, destination or connection point.

That makes the activity relevant to operators building regular mobility around workplaces, neighbourhoods, schools and transport gateways. It can be registered at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. The scope is specific about the services it embraces, while drawing one clear boundary: ambulance transportation is outside it. For an operator, the category therefore describes recurring, purpose-built passenger movement rather than a catch-all label for every kind of road journey.

Across Indonesia, the foreign-investment position is clear. For this activity, TERBUKA status sets the foreign-ownership ceiling at 100%. In other words, foreign ownership may reach the full national ceiling for this activity. The applicable PMA source recorded here is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national openness matters, but it should not be mistaken for a generic statement about every operating context; the Bali picture is recorded separately and deserves to be read on its own terms.

In Bali, this activity is not blocked by the province-wide PMA moratorium. The stated rule blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island on a permanent basis. Here, the recorded Bali position is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: at Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so the activity is not caught by that moratorium. For a foreign investor considering Bali, that is the honest conclusion from this record: the activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not blocked there by the stated low-risk and medium-low-risk PMA restriction.
